The Delhi government is set to introduce Individual Aftercare Plans (IAPs) for teenagers exiting Child Care Institutions (CCIs) at 18, based on their specific circumstances, requirements and rehabilitation needs, under the proposed ‘Aftercare Scheme for Young Persons’, a senior government official said on Sunday.
Under the scheme, the eligible beneficiaries will receive up to ₹2 lakh for higher education and ₹60,000 for vocational training.
The scheme is likely to be approved by the Delhi Cabinet soon, according to a senior government official.
In May, the Women and Child Development Department proposed a budget of ₹3.50 crore for the implementation of the scheme for the current financial year. The government also plans to allocate ₹5 crore from the Chief Minister’s Development Fund to strengthen the juvenile justice system, including the aftercare scheme, the official said.
The government is also seeking Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partnerships to provide mentorship, additional financial resources, and other forms of support.
The scheme will be implemented under a two-tier structure where the District Aftercare Committees will assess eligibility, map out individual plans, and track beneficiary progress, and the State Aftercare Committees will oversee the implementation, fund disbursement and policy reforms.
“There will also be a provision for financial assistance, subject to the recommendation of the District Aftercare Committee, for eligible young people who have no income or insufficient income,” the official said.
“A database of individuals eligible for aftercare will be maintained and these individuals will be recommended to various Delhi government departments for internships, contractual roles, or outsourced employment opportunities, provided they meet the prescribed eligibility criteria,” the official added.
Under the scheme, the government will start preparations when a child in a CCI is 15 years old, with focus on acquiring the skills necessary for living independently. By the time they turn 17, officials will evaluate their readiness and specific support needs.
“Post 18 years, the aftercare support will cover education, training, housing, financial assistance, mentorship and employment, based on an individualised aftercare plan,” the official said.
Delhi currently has around 88 CCIs operated jointly by the government and various non-governmental organisations. These homes provide care, protection, education and rehabilitation to children up to the age of 18. Every year, between 150 and 200 young adults exit these institutions after turning 18, according to officials.
As per the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, support is generally provided up to the age of 21. However, in exceptional circumstances, and upon the recommendation of competent bodies, it may be extended up to the age of 23, the official added.
